:::{#def-real-numbers}
#### Real numbers

A **real number**
[@wikipedia_real_number]
is a number that can be written as a decimal expansion:
an integer part, followed by a decimal point
and a finite or infinite list of decimal places after it.
Equivalently, the real numbers are the points on the number line.
The set of real numbers is written $\reals$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-real-numbers-working-definition}
#### A working definition

@def-real-numbers is a working definition, not a construction:
it does not say what an infinite decimal expansion is,
or how to add or multiply two of them.
@rudin1976principles [Appendix to Chapter 1] constructs the real numbers rigorously.
Some real numbers have two decimal expansions:
for example, $0.999\ldots$ and $1.000\ldots$ are the same real number, $1$.

:::
